% Converted, ltx-talk. C-FRAMESUBTITLE workaround: fold both parts into a single
% \frametitle through a preamble macro, so the subtitle text actually reaches the
% page. Defining \frametitlesub (rather than redefining \framesubtitle) keeps the
% deck off ltx-talk's private internals, and lets a Beamer-side preamble define
% the same macro as a real \frametitle + \framesubtitle pair -- so the deck stays
% exportable back to Beamer.
%
% This is a documented upstream gap, not a class bug: ltx-talk.pdf says the frame
% subtitle "is not used in output: this will be addressed in later releases".
% Retire this macro once it is.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard=a-4, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}

\newcommand{\frametitlesub}[2]{\frametitle{#1 --- {\normalsize #2}}}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}[c]
\frametitlesub{Constraint Satisfaction}{Quiz}
Body text.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
